title: Protocol to isolate RBP-mRNA complexes using RNA-CLIP and examine target mRNAs
protocol: Set up a peristaltic pump at 3.5 mL/min as perfusion flow rate.
Wash the tubing of the pump with 70% Ethanol.
Wash the tubing of the pump with PBS.
Wash the tubing of the pump with perfusion medium.
Place Perfusion medium and Digest medium in a water bath set at 37°C.
Keep Leibovitz’s L-15 medium in ice until receiving the dissected liver.
Anesthetize the mouse.
Position the anesthetized mouse on a dissecting board, belly up.
Sanitize the abdomen with 70% ethanol.
Perform a midline ventral incision with large blade scissors.
Pull aside the flap of skin to expose the body wall.
Make an incision into the peritoneum with fine blade scissors to expose the liver.
Cannulate the vena cava with a 22-gauge iv catheter.
Perfuse the liver with perfusion medium for 10 min.
Perfuse the liver with Digest medium containing 0.05% Collagenase in perfusion medium.
Isolate the liver after digestion for 6-7 minutes.
Remove the gall bladder from the isolated liver.
Using fine blade scissors, dissociate the liver from the diaphragm.
Using fine blade scissors, dissociate the liver from the esophagus.
Using fine blade scissors, dissociate the liver from the stomach.
Using fine blade scissors, dissociate the liver from the kidney.
Using fine blade scissors, dissociate the liver from the small intestine.
Place the liver in a 15 mL plastic conical tube containing 15 mL of Leibovitz’s L-15 medium supplemented with 5% FBS and 1% penicillin-streptomycin mix.
Manually disrupt the liver using a rubber cell scraper, keeping the tube on ice.
Pipette up and down through a 25 mL serological pipet followed by 2–3 passages through a 10 mL pipet to further disaggregate tissue clumps.
Filter the suspension through a 100 μm nylon cell strainer into a new 50 mL tube on ice.
Spin at 50 × g for 5 minutes at 4°C.
Wash the pellet twice with 30 mL hepatocyte wash medium, spinning at 50 × g for 5 minutes between each wash.
Resuspend the hepatocytes in 10 mL of fresh medium after the final wash.
Count cell number and determine viability using Trypan blue.
Wash the monolayer of primary hepatocytes twice with 4 mL ice-cold PBS.
Remove the liquid and place the dishes without their cover on a layer of ice in a Stratalinker 2400.
Irradiate the dishes with 400 mj/cm² of 254 nm UV light.
Scrape the hepatocytes in 1 ml NP-40 complete lysis buffer.
Incubate the scraped cells for 5 minutes on ice.
Freeze the cells at -80°C to promote lysis.
Scrape cells in 2 mL ice cold PBS containing protease and phosphatase inhibitors after irradiation.
Spin the cell suspension at 300 × g for 5 min at 4°C.
Resuspend the pellet in 1 mL cold PBS and transfer into a 1.5 mL Eppendorf tube.
Keep the tube on ice.
Spin the sample at 300 × g for 5 min.
Aspirate the supernatant, leaving a thin layer of liquid to prevent the cell pellet from drying.
Store the pellet at -80°C until further processing.
Thaw lysates on ice and complete lysis by homogenizing with a glass Dounce and Pestle B (tight).
Perform 20 strokes up and down for homogenization.
Check efficiency of lysis under microscope.
If unbroken cells remain, perform two additional strokes and check again.
When starting from frozen cell pellets, thaw the pellet on ice.
Wash the pellet once with cold PBS, spin at 300 × g, remove PBS, resuspend cells in Complete NP-40 Lysis buffer.
Proceed with Dounce homogenization.
Wash freshly harvested livers twice with 10 mL chilled PBS.
Mince the liver with a razor blade.
Cover minced pieces of liver with 1–2 mL chilled PBS and place on ice.
Expose minced liver to 400 mj/cm² of 254 nm UV irradiation in three cycles.
Collect minced liver by centrifugation at 380 × g.
Resuspend the liver fragments in complete NP-40 lysis buffer.
Homogenize using a glass Dounce and Pestle A (loose) for 20 strokes followed by 20 strokes with Pestle B (tight).
Centrifuge the lysate at 13,000 × g for 15 min at 4°C to clear the lysate.
Incubate lysates with RNaseOUT (3 μL/mL lysate) for 5 min on ice.
Treat lysates with RQ1 DNAse (30 μL/mL lysate) for 5 min at 37°C, gently mixing every 2 minutes.
Add 0.5M EDTA (4 μL/mL lysate) to chelate Mg²⁺ which inhibits RNase T1 and add RNase T1 (0.3 μL/mL lysate).
Incubate bound RNA digestion mixture at 24°C for 15 min.
Place the mixture on ice after incubation.
Dilute lysate 1:1 with NDE buffer containing proteases and phosphatase inhibitors.
Keep diluted lysate on ice until immunoprecipitation is undertaken.
Use a magnetic tube rack to handle ChIP-Grade Protein G Magnetic beads.
Wash appropriate volume of beads (50 μL per mL lysate) twice with 10 volumes of NT2 buffer by inverting the tubes three times.
Resuspend beads in 5 volumes of NT2 buffer supplemented with 5 mg/mL BSA and 0.2 mg/mL yeast tRNA.
Incubate resuspended beads at 4°C for 1 hour to block beads and minimize non-specific binding.
Wash the beads twice with 10–20 volumes of NT2 buffer.
Resuspend the beads in 10 volumes of 1× NDE buffer.
Dilute beads (40 μL/mL lysate) into 5 volumes of NT2 buffer supplemented with 1 mg/mL BSA and 0.2 mg/mL yeast tRNA.
Add anti-FLAG antibody (4 μg/40 μL beads).
Incubate with constant rotation for 4 h at 4°C.
Wash antibody-bound beads twice with 10–20 volumes of NT2 buffer.
Mix the beads in solution, away from the magnet.
Add antibody-bound beads (40 μL) to 2 mL diluted cell lysates.
Incubate 14 h at 4°C under constant rotation.
Capture the beads using magnetic tube rack.
Wash the beads twice with 1 mL NT2 buffer.
Wash the beads twice with 1 mL high salt NT2 buffer.
Capture the beads and aspirate the remaining wash buffer.
Resuspend the RBP complexes-bound beads into 100 μL RNase T1 mix (1× RNaseT1 buffer, 2 μL RNaseOUT, 1.6 U/μL final RNase T1).
Incubate 15 min at 25°C.
Place on ice for 5 min.
Add 1 mL of high salt NT2 buffer.
Separate the beads.
Wash twice with high salt NT2 buffer.
Resuspend washed beads in 50 μL CIP reaction mix (1× CIP buffer, 0.2 U RNaseOUT, 0.5 U/μL CIP).
Incubate for 10 minutes at 37°C with periodic gentle mixing.
Add 1 mL of CIP wash buffer.
Separate the beads.
Wash twice with CIP wash buffer.
Wash twice with PNK wash buffer.
Remove all wash buffer after the last wash.
Ligate RL3-Biotin primer by incubating beads in 50 μL ligation mix (1× ligase buffer, 0.2 U RNaseOUT, 20 pmol RL3-biotin primer, 12.5 U T4 RNA ligase) at 25°C for 2 hours.
Add 1 mL PNK wash buffer and separate the beads.
Wash once with 1 mL PNK wash buffer.
Resuspend the beads in 100 μL of PNK mix containing 1× ligase buffer, 0.2 U RNaseOUT and 25 U T4 PNK and incubate at 37°C for 20 min.
Add 1 mL of PNK wash buffer and separate the beads.
Remove solution.
Resuspend in 50 μL ligation reaction containing RL5a-TYE705 RNA adapter and incubate at 25°C for 2 h.
Wash once in 1 mL NT2 buffer.
Wash once with high salt NT2 buffer.
Wash three times with 2 mL PNK wash buffer.
Completely remove the last wash buffer.
Resuspend the beads in 40 μL of 1× SDS-PAGE loading buffer.
Denature and release RBP complexes by heating the beads for 5 min at 95°C.
Place Eppendorf tubes on magnetic tube rack to remove beads.
Collect supernatant and load onto a 4–12 Bis-Tris Novex gel.
Run gel at 180 V for 90 min at 4°C.
Transfer RNP complexes with 1× MOPS transfer buffer containing 10% methanol onto nitrocellulose membrane for 2h30 min at 33V.
Mark the membrane with a chemically resistant marker at upper and lower right corner for orientation.
Wash the membrane with 10 mL PBS.
Visualize labeled RNP complexes using Licor Odyssey at 700 nm.
Capture and print TIFF images.
Line up images and membrane, excise areas of nitrocellulose overlapping the labeled RNP complexes.
Pre-incubate 11 μg of tRNA (220 ng/μL final) with 11 Units of RQ1-DNase in 50 μL for 30 min at 37°C.
Add 5 μL of 20 mM EGTA to inactivate DNase.
Prepare a PK solution by diluting tRNA 1:8.
Dilute proteinase K 1:5 to a final concentration of 2 mg/mL in 1× PK buffer.
Incubate the PK solution at 37°C for 30 min.
Incubate pieces of nitrocellulose with 200 μL RNAse-free PK solution at 55°C with agitation on a rotating wheel for 20 min.
Add 200 μL of 50 mM Tris and 100 mM NaCl to the incubated samples and incubate at 37°C for 20 min.
Dilute tRNA in PK buffer to prepare a final concentration of 25 ng/μL.
Vortex the mixture for 1 minute.
Centrifuge at max speed (16,800 × g) at 24°C for 5 minutes.
Collect the aqueous phase and add an equal volume of chloroform.
Vortex for 30 seconds, then centrifuge at 16,800 × g for 5 minutes.
Add one-tenth volume of 3M Na-Acetate pH 5 to the collected aqueous phase.
Add three volumes of ethanol and vortex thoroughly.
Precipitate the mixture at −20°C for 14 hours or at −80°C for 1 hour.
Centrifuge at maximum speed (16,800 × g) in a refrigerated centrifuge for 30 minutes at 4°C.
Wash the pellet with 75% ethanol (100 μL).
Spin at maximum speed (16,800 × g) for 10 minutes and remove the supernatant.
Air-dry the pellet for 10 minutes at 24°C.
Resuspend the dried pellet in 11.5 μL RNAse-free H2O.
Mix RNA with dNTPs to a final volume of 13 μL.
Heat the mixture at 65°C for 5 minutes.
Place the heated mixture on ice for 1 minute.
Add DTT, 5× first strand buffer, RNaseOUT, and Superscript III enzyme to achieve a total reaction volume of 20 μL.
Incubate in a thermocycler at 50°C for 45 minutes.
Continue incubation at 55°C for 15 minutes.
Further incubate at 70°C for 15 minutes and then store the cDNA at 4°C.
Combine 2 μL of cDNA with DP5a and DP3 primers in a 25 μL reaction containing dNTPs and 0.5 Units Platinum Pfx DNA polymerase.
Place the reaction in a thermocycler for PCR amplification according to specified parameters.
Gel purify PCR products on a 2.3% agarose gel following Qiagen Gel extraction procedure.
Use an aliquot of purified PCR products (50 ng) for a second round of amplification with DSFP5a and RPIX-D3 primers in a 25 μL reaction.
Purification of PCR products can be performed using any DNA cleanup system, such as AMPure XP or PureLink Quick Gel Extraction kit.
Anesthetize the mouse with ketamine and xylazine followed by cervical dislocation.
Secure the animal on a dissecting board with pins.
Sanitize the abdomen with 70% ethanol.
Hold the skin with forceps and perform a midline ventral incision with large blade scissors.
Pull aside the flap of the skin to expose the body wall.
Make an incision with fine blade scissor to expose the internal abdominal organs.
Unfold the small intestine and carefully displace outside the ventral cavity.
Remove the entire small intestine from the gastro-duodenal junction proximally to the ileo-cecal junction and colon at its distal end.
Place the entire small intestine on a petri dish containing 5 mL ice-cold PBS.
Open the intestine longitudinally along the antimesenteric border.
Wash the intestine twice with 5 mL cold PBS.
Incubate in 5 mL PBS supplemented with 100 μg/mL cycloheximide for 5 min on ice.
Scrape the mucosa with gentle compression using a glass slide.
Resuspend the scraped mucosa in 1 mL cold polysome lysis buffer (PLB).
Keep the resuspended tissue into a 1.7 mL Eppendorf tube on ice for 5–15 min.
Follow the same steps to identify and remove the five liver lobes.
Remove the gallbladder and dissect out the liver.
Place the liver in a petri dish on ice and wash twice in 10 mL cold PBS.
Cut the liver lobes into 0.5 cm pieces with fine blade scissors.
Incubate the liver pieces in 10 mL ice-cold PBS supplemented with 100 μg/mL cycloheximide for 5 min on ice.
Mince the liver pieces with a razor blade.
Transfer the finely minced liver into a 2 mL Eppendorf tube.
Incubate in 1.2 mL cold PLB on ice for 5-15 minutes.
Disrupt the tissue in a chilled 2 mL Dounce glass tissue grinder.
Perform 20 strokes with pestle A followed by 20 strokes with pestle B to prepare liver extract.
Verify complete cell disruption by examining an aliquot of the extract under a light microscope.
Evaluate the volume of extract after initial homogenization.
Add 10% Triton X-100 to achieve a final concentration of 1% in the extract.
Perform 10 additional strokes with pestle B.
Centrifuge the extracts at 10,000 × g for 10 minutes at 4°C.
Load cleared extract on top of a 10%–50% sucrose gradient (∼750 μL per 12 mL gradient).
Prepare the stock sucrose gradient buffer the day before use.
Add DTT and cycloheximide to the stock sucrose gradient buffer the day of use.
Pipette 6 mL of complete 50% sucrose buffer into each polypropylene centrifuge tube (Beckman).
Add the upper complete 10% sucrose buffer layer by placing the pipette tip against the side of the tube and slowly pipetting down the solution.
Secure a capillary cap on top of the tube with Parafilm.
Level the MagnaBase tube holder using a bubble level.
Press the keys [Recall] [0] followed by keys [1], [4], and [7] to adjust 0.1, 1, and 10 degrees up respectively.
Press the keys [3], [6], and [9] for similar degrees down.
Load 6 mL of 50% sucrose gradient buffer at the bottom of the ultracentrifugation tube.
Slowly load 6 mL of 10% sucrose gradient buffer.
Observe the interphase between the two solutions as the tube is moved slowly.
Close the ultracentrifugation tube with a capillary cap and secure it with parafilm.
Enter parameters for time, angle, and speed of rotation.
Start the run on the gradient maker.
The Magnabase moves to the first set angle and starts rotating.
Place the centrifuge tubes in the tube holder and set the gradient maker for time, angle, and speed of rotation of the tube holder.
Run cycle 1: 5 s/87º/30 rpm.
Repeat cycles 1 and 2 consecutively five times.
Run cycle 2: 15 s/87º/0 rpm.
Run cycle 3: 19 s/80º/20 rpm.
Keep the gradients at 4°C until the extracts are ready for loading.
Let the gradients thaw at 4°C overnight before use.

Gently and slowly load lysates (∼750 μL) on top of each centrifuge tube using a P1000 pipette tip held at a 45° angle to the meniscus of the sucrose solution against the wall of the centrifuge tube, pipetting down slowly.
Balance paired tubes with lysis buffer.
Close the buckets with their respective caps and place them in the ultracentrifuge chamber.
Spin the samples at 261,000 × g for 2 hours and 15 minutes at 4°C.
Prepare 13 × 2 mL Eppendorf tubes marked to indicate 900 μL and keep them on ice.
Remove centrifuge tube from its bucket and place it on a tube holder.
Pierce the base of the centrifuge tube using a 26-gauge needle.
Slowly remove the needle and start collecting fractions from the bottom of the tube, keeping the fractions on ice.
Use a NANODrop instrument to read absorbance at 260 nm for each fraction after blanking the spectrophotometer with water.
To each fraction add 1 volume (900 μL) of 8M guanidine HCl.
Add 1/10 volume (90 μL) sodium acetate 3M pH 5.2 to each fraction.
Add 1 μL glycogen (∼20 μg) to each fraction.
Split each fraction into two 2 mL Eppendorf tubes, each containing 900 μL.
Add one volume (900 μL) of phenol: chloroform: IAA (125:24:1) pH4 to each tube.
Vortex for 10 seconds and incubate on ice for 15 minutes.
Spin at 14,000 rpm for 20 minutes at 4°C.
Collect the aqueous phase and add one volume (900 μL) of isopropanol.
Vortex and incubate at -20°C for 14 hours.
Precipitate RNA by centrifuging at 4°C for 20 minutes at 16,800 × g.
Wash with 50 μL of 75% ethanol.
Combine identical fractions.
Spin the resulting 13 fractions for 15 minutes at 4°C at 16,800 × g.
Air dry for 10 minutes at 24°C, open cap and resuspend in 100 μL water.
Add 7.5M LiCl to a final concentration of 2M.
Vortex and incubate at -20°C or -80°C for 30 minutes.
Spin down the RNA at 16,800 × g for 20 min at 4°C.
Wash the RNA pellet with 50 μl 75% Ethanol.
Spin at 16,800 × g for 15 min at 4°C.
Remove the supernatant and air dry for 10 min at 24°C.
Resuspend the RNA in 20 μL water.
